headline: The Real Dan Sullivan
dek: A week after the midterms, the President says Senator Dan Sullivan won in Alaska, claims that a second candidate of the same name was put up by the Democrats for fraud and confusion, and asks that those votes be given to the senator. He offers no evidence in the post.

original.speaker: Donald J. Trump
text: Dan Sullivan PLUS Dan Sullivan wins the Alaska Election by thousands of votes. All votes going to the Fake Dan Sullivan, which was done solely for the purpose of fraud and confusion, should immediately be given to the Real Dan Sullivan (Senator!) - Likewise the votes of the second fraudulent candidate, also put up by the Dems. There should be no question concerning this Rigged Election. Time is of the essence!!! President DJT
original.key: All votes going to the Fake Dan Sullivan, which was done solely for the purpose of fraud and confusion, should immediately be given to the Real Dan Sullivan (Senator!)
original.context: Posted on 10 November 2026, a week after the midterm elections of 3 November. Dan Sullivan is the Republican senator for Alaska; the President refers to a second candidate of the same name on the ballot, and to another candidate he calls fraudulent.

verification.note: Copied by the editor from truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump on 10 November 2026 (shown as 11/10/26, 4:36 AM Pacific).

en: Senator Dan Sullivan is the candidate Alaskans know, and I believe he has their support.

If voters were misled by another candidate with the same name, election officials and, if necessary, the courts should look into it promptly, under Alaska law. Every lawful vote must be counted as it was cast.
fr: Le sénateur Dan Sullivan est le candidat que les Alaskiens connaissent, et je crois qu’il a leur soutien.

Si des électeurs ont été trompés par un autre candidat portant le même nom, les responsables électoraux et, si nécessaire, les tribunaux doivent l’examiner rapidement, selon la loi de l’Alaska. Chaque vote légal doit être compté tel qu’il a été exprimé.
presidential.key: If voters were misled by another candidate with the same name, election officials should look into it promptly. Every lawful vote must be counted as it was cast.

vaudois.hook: Il y a un faux Dan Sullivan ! *Chez nous, il y a trois Pittet par village.*
vaudois.hookEn: There’s a fake Dan Sullivan! *Round here there are three Pittets in every village.*
vaudois.short: Chez nous, il y a trois Pittet par village : celui du haut, celui de la poste, celui de la laiterie. *Personne ne s’est jamais trompé de Pittet.*
vaudois.shortEn: Round here every village has three Pittets: the one up the hill, the post-office one, the dairy one. *Nobody ever votes for the wrong Pittet.*
text: Le vrai Dan Sullivan a gagné en Alaska, et de loin. Les voix du faux Dan Sullivan, qui est là, je le dis, pour embrouiller les gens, il faut les rendre au vrai. Tout de suite.

Remarquez, chez nous, il y a trois Pittet par village : le Pittet du haut, le Pittet de la poste et le Pittet de la laiterie. Et personne ne s’est jamais trompé de Pittet. Alors on va voir. Mais tranquillement, hein.
en: The real Dan Sullivan won in Alaska, and by a mile. The votes for the fake Dan Sullivan, who is there, I say, just to confuse people, must go back to the real one. Right away.

Mind you, round here every village has three Pittets: the Pittet up the hill, the post-office Pittet and the dairy Pittet. And nobody has ever voted for the wrong Pittet. So we’ll see. But no rush, eh.
notes: Pittet is one of the most common surnames in the canton of Vaud; in a village, namesakes are told apart by where they live or what they do.

neuchatelois.hook: Un faux Dan Sullivan ! *Chez nous, une fausse montre, on la reconnaît à l’œil.*
neuchatelois.hookEn: A fake Dan Sullivan! *Round here we spot a fake watch at a glance.*
neuchatelois.short: Chez nous, une contrefaçon, on la reconnaît à la loupe : le mouvement, le poinçon, le tic-tac. *Les électeurs aussi ont une loupe.*
neuchatelois.shortEn: Round here we spot a fake watch under the magnifying glass: the movement, the hallmark, the tick. *Voters have a magnifying glass too.*
text: Dan Sullivan, le vrai, a gagné en Alaska avec des milliers de voix d’avance. Le faux Dan Sullivan, c’est une contrefaçon, je le dis, faite pour tromper, et ses voix doivent revenir au vrai.

Bon, chez nous, une contrefaçon, on la reconnaît à la loupe : le mouvement, le poinçon, le tic-tac. Une fausse montre ne trompe pas un horloger. Remarquez, un électeur non plus, en général. C’est un peu ce qui m’inquiète.
en: Dan Sullivan, the real one, won in Alaska by thousands of votes. The fake Dan Sullivan is a counterfeit, I say, made to fool people, and his votes must go back to the real one.

Well, round here we spot a counterfeit under the magnifying glass: the movement, the hallmark, the tick. A fake watch never fools a watchmaker. Mind you, it doesn’t usually fool a voter either. That’s rather what worries me.
notes: The Neuchâtel mountains are the heart of Swiss watchmaking, and the Swiss watch industry fights counterfeits fiercely; a watchmaker checks a watch with a loupe.

breton.hook: Le faux Dan Sullivan ! *C’est comme le beurre doux : fait pour embrouiller.*
breton.hookEn: The fake Dan Sullivan! *Like unsalted butter: made to confuse people.*
breton.short: Chez nous, il y a le vrai beurre, le salé, et le doux, qui ressemble au vrai pour embrouiller les gens. *On n’a jamais rendu le doux au salé.*
breton.shortEn: Here the real butter is salted; unsalted looks like it, to confuse people. *We never handed it over, though.*
text: Le vrai Dan Sullivan a gagné en Alaska. Le faux, on l’a mis là, je le dis, pour embrouiller les électeurs, et ses voix doivent revenir au vrai.

Chez nous, c’est pareil avec le beurre : il y a le vrai, le salé, et le doux, qui lui ressemble pour semer la confusion. Mais on a beau râler, on n’a jamais rendu le doux au salé. Chacun garde ce qu’on lui a mis dans la crêpe.
en: The real Dan Sullivan won in Alaska. The fake one was put there, I say, to confuse voters, and his votes must go back to the real one.

Here it’s the same with butter: there’s the real one, salted, and the unsalted one, which looks like it to confuse people. But grumble as we may, we’ve never handed the unsalted butter over to the salted. Each keeps what was put in his crêpe.
notes: In Brittany, salted butter is a matter of identity; unsalted butter is viewed with polite suspicion.

parisien.hook: Un faux Dan Sullivan ! *À Paris, les faux, on les vend au Trocadéro.*
parisien.hookEn: A fake Dan Sullivan! *In Paris, fakes are sold at the Trocadéro.*
parisien.short: À Paris, les faux, on connaît : la tour Eiffel en plastique au Trocadéro, le sac de luxe sur un drap. *Mais on n’a jamais rendu l’argent au vrai.*
parisien.shortEn: In Paris we know fakes: plastic Eiffel Towers at the Trocadéro, luxury bags on a sheet. *But nobody ever paid the real one back.*
text: Le vrai Dan Sullivan a gagné en Alaska, et de loin. Le faux, c’est une arnaque, je le dis, et ses voix doivent aller au vrai, tout de suite, parce que le temps presse.

À Paris, les faux, on connaît : la tour Eiffel en plastique au Trocadéro, le sac de luxe sur un drap qu’on replie quand la police arrive. Mais personne n’a jamais demandé qu’on rende l’argent au vrai. Bon, j’ai pas le temps, j’ai un rendez-vous.
en: The real Dan Sullivan won in Alaska, by a mile. The fake one is a scam, I say, and his votes must go to the real one, right now, because time is short.

In Paris we know fakes: plastic Eiffel Towers at the Trocadéro, luxury bags on a sheet that gets folded up when the police arrive. But nobody ever asked for the money to go to the real brand. Right, I’ve no time, I’ve got a meeting.
notes: Street sellers of souvenirs and counterfeit goods are a familiar sight around the Trocadéro, opposite the Eiffel Tower.

california.hook: A fake Dan Sullivan! *In LA we call that a stunt double.*
california.short: In Hollywood, every star has a stunt double who looks just like him. *And the double never gets the credits. Or the votes.*
text: So the real Dan Sullivan totally won Alaska, by thousands of votes. And this other Dan Sullivan? Fake, I’m telling you, just there to confuse people. His votes should go to the real one. Like, now.
Honestly, in LA we have a word for that: a stunt double. Same face, same jacket, does the falls. But the double never gets the credits. Or the votes, apparently.
en: He says the senator won by thousands of votes, calls the other candidate with the same name a fake meant to confuse voters, and wants his votes transferred: claims he makes without evidence.
In Hollywood terms, the namesake is a “stunt double”, who looks like the star but never gets the credit.

midwest.hook: Two Dan Sullivans! *Back home we just say “Dan, no, the other Dan.”*
midwest.short: Back home there are four Ole Johnsons at every church supper. *We just say “Ole, no, the other Ole,” and pass the hotdish.*
text: Well, I don’t want to make a fuss, but the real Dan Sullivan won up there in Alaska, by a good bit. And this other Dan Sullivan, I’d say he’s just there to mix folks up. Those votes ought to go to the real Dan, if it’s not too much trouble.
Back home, there are four Ole Johnsons at every church supper. We just say “Ole, no, the other Ole,” and pass the hotdish. Nobody ever asked to move the votes around. But hey, different state.
en: Very politely, he claims the senator won, suggests the namesake is there to confuse voters, and asks that the votes be moved to him.
In the Upper Midwest, Scandinavian names such as Johnson are so common that namesakes are routine; “hotdish” is the casserole of every church supper.

manchester.hook: There’s a fake Dan Sullivan! *We’ve two clubs here. Nobody mixes them up.*
manchester.short: Manchester’s had two big clubs for over a century, both called Manchester. *Nobody’s ever cheered for the wrong one by mistake.*
text: The real Dan Sullivan won Alaska by thousands, to be fair. The other Dan Sullivan’s a fake, I’m telling you, there to confuse people, and his votes should go to the real one. Sharpish.
Mind, this city’s had two big clubs for over a century, both called Manchester, both in red or blue. Nobody’s ever cheered for the wrong one by mistake. People tend to know what they meant.
en: He says the senator won by thousands, calls the namesake a fake, and wants his votes moved to the senator, quickly (“sharpish”).
Manchester has two famous football clubs, United (red) and City (blue): supporters never mix them up, so voters may not have either.

british-diplomat.hook: Give the votes to the Real Dan Sullivan! *Voters usually know who they meant.*
british-diplomat.short: Our ballot papers print each candidate’s party next to the name, precisely so that namesakes can be told apart. *It generally works.*
british-diplomat.shortEn: He thinks some votes went to the wrong Dan Sullivan. *The voters may disagree.*
text: His Majesty’s Government has noted the President’s concern about two candidates sharing a name in Alaska.
Our own ballot papers print each candidate’s party or description next to the name, precisely so that namesakes can be told apart. In our experience, voters generally know which one they meant.
en: He thinks some votes went to the wrong Dan Sullivan.
He would like them moved. The voters may feel they put them where they wanted.

text: France has full confidence in the American institutions that count and certify the vote.
In France, a ballot counts for the name printed on it, and for no other; disputes go to the judge of the election. It is sometimes frustrating, and always reassuring.
fr: La France a pleine confiance dans les institutions américaines qui comptent et certifient le vote.
En France, un bulletin compte pour le nom qu’il porte, et pour aucun autre ; les contestations vont au juge de l’élection. C’est parfois frustrant, et toujours rassurant.
notes: In France, disputes over an election are decided by a court, “le juge de l’élection”: the administrative courts for local elections, the Constitutional Council for parliamentary and presidential ones.

text: The Federal Council takes note of the President’s concerns.

In Switzerland, namesakes are common: on our lists for the National Council, each candidate appears with first name, year of birth, profession and place of residence. Voters choose; nobody moves their votes afterwards.
fr: Le Conseil fédéral prend acte des préoccupations du Président.

En Suisse, les homonymes sont fréquents : sur nos listes pour le Conseil national, chaque candidat figure avec son prénom, son année de naissance, sa profession et son domicile. Les électeurs choisissent ; personne ne déplace leurs voix ensuite.
